references.text: The Lord promised Abraham that Sarah would have a son
God announces the birth of Isaac to Abraham
God blesses Sarah and promises she will become the mother of nations
God sets the time for Isaac's birth
Sarah was enabled to conceive by faith because she trusted in Him who had made the promise
Paul refers to Abraham's faith and God's promise of a son
God is not human, so He does not lie; He does what He has said—a principle fulfilled in Genesis 21:1
Confirms the historical fulfillment of the promise of a son to Sarah in her old age.
A parallel in God's faithfulness by fulfilling His word despite impossible circumstances.
A direct linguistic and theological parallel regarding God's ability to fulfill His word.
An allusion to Sarah as an example of faith in the Lord's promise and its fulfillment.
A direct quotation of the promise that was fulfilled in Genesis 21:1.
A theological parallel concerning God's nature as 'the One who sees' and intervenes in human destiny.
A direct prophetic precursor raising the question of God's power, which verse 21:1 answers.
Theological confirmation of God's power to fulfill the promise of a son.
Theological principle of God's faithfulness that supports the fulfillment of the promise.
